'''Olga Dmitrievna Ulyanova''' ({{Langx|ru|Ольга Дмитриевна Ульянова}}; 4 March 1922 – 25 March 2011) was a Russian chemist, physicist, and writer. The niece of [[Vladimir Lenin]], she was one of his last-known living relatives before her death. Ulyanova was a supporter of Lenin's legacy, writing extensively about her uncle and family. She was awarded the [[Order of the Red Banner of Labour]] by the [[Soviet Union]] for her writing. Ulyanova actively campaigned for Lenin's body to stay in [[Lenin's Mausoleum]] during discussions of reburying it outside of the [[Red Square]]. While supportive of maintaining Lenin's legacy, she told European press that it was a mistake to make him into an icon.

== Biography ==
Olga Ulyanova was born in Moscow on 4 March 1922, the daughter of the Russian physician and revolutionary [[Dmitry Ilyich Ulyanov]] and Antonia Ivanovna Neshcheretova.<ref name= boston>{{cite web|url=https://archive.boston.com/bostonglobe/obituaries/articles/2011/03/26/olga_ulyanova_89_niece_protective_of_lenins_legacy/ |title=Olga Ulyanova, 89, niece protective of Lenin's legacy - The Boston Globe |publisher=Archive.boston.com |date=2011-03-26 |accessdate=2022-08-24}}</ref> She had a brother, Viktor.<ref>{{cite news|title=Viktor Ulyanov Dies in Soviet; Lenin Nephew Was Engineer|url=https://www.nytimes.com/1984/12/05/obituaries/viktor-ulyanov-dies-in-soviet-lenin-nephew-was-engineer.html/|website=[[The New York Times]]|date=5 December 1984|accessdate=8 October 2015}}</ref> Ulyanova's father was the brother of [[Vladimir Lenin]], [[Aleksandr Ulyanov]], [[Anna Ulyanova]], [[Olga Ilyinichna Ulyanova]], and [[Maria Ilyinichna Ulyanova]]. Her grandfather, [[Ilya Ulyanov|Ilya Nikolayevich Ulyanov]], was an educator who was promoted to the rank of [[Active State Councillor]], thus granting the family the privilege of [[Russian nobility|hereditary nobility]].<ref name="uniros">{{cite web|title=Владимир Ильич Ленин (1870–1924)|url=http://www.uniros.ru/articles/lenin.php|publisher=Uniros.ru|access-date=24 August 2022|language=Russian|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://archive.today/20120918123515/http://www.uniros.ru/articles/lenin.php|archive-date=18 September 2012}}</ref> Her grandmother, [[Maria Alexandrovna Ulyanova]], was a member of the [[Blank family]].

Ulyanova grew up in the [[Kremlin]], surrounded by children of other [[Bolshevik]] leaders.<ref name= boston/>

In 1991, following the collapse of the [[Soviet Union]], there was discussion of moving Lenin's preserved body from [[Lenin's Mausoleum|his tomb]] on [[Red Square]] to [[Kremlin Wall Necropolis]] or [[Volkovo Cemetery]]. Ulyanova fiercely objected to the discussion, believing that Lenin's body belonged at Red Square, and campaigned for the body to stay there.<ref name= boston/><ref name= reuters/> In 2007, she told [[Interfax|Interfax News Agency]] that "those who want his reburial are just malefactors."<ref name= boston/> 

In 2008, Ulyanova told ''[[Panorama (magazine)|Panorama]]'' that "it was a mistake to turn [Lenin] into an icon", saying that "ideological distortions, falsification of his theories were even a bigger mistake."<ref name= boston/> She maintained the position that her uncle disapproved of the [[execution of the Romanov family]].<ref name= boston/>

Ulyanova, a chemist and physicist, worked as professor of chemistry and physics at various Russian universities.<ref name= boston/> She also wrote multiple books about Lenin.<ref name= boston/><ref>{{cite news | url=https://www.thetimes.com/comment/register/article/olga-ulyanova-bgxdxz7vt0j | title=Olga Ulyanova }}</ref> She was awarded the [[Order of the Red Banner of Labour]] for her writing.

She died in Moscow on 25 March 2011.<ref>{{cite news |author=<!-- not stated --> |url=https://www.inquirer.com/philly/obituaries/20110328_Olga_Ulyanova___Lenin_s_niece__89.html |title=Olga Ulyanova; Lenin's niece, 89 |newspaper=The Philadelphia Inquirer |date=2011-03-28 |access-date=2025-07-31}}</ref> According to the government in [[Ulyanovsk Oblast]], Ulyanova was one of the last known living relatives of Lenin.<ref name= reuters>{{cite news | url=https://www.reuters.com/article/idINIndia-55890320110325 | title=Last relative of Soviet founder Lenin dies aged 89 | newspaper=Reuters | date=25 March 2011 }}</ref>
